metadata.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding (Devlin et al., 2018)
metadata.framework: Pre-training deep bidirectional Transformer representations via masked language modeling and next sentence prediction
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on arXiv:1810.04805 PDF text.

nodes.name: BERT model architecture
nodes.statement: BERT is a multi-layer bidirectional Transformer encoder based on the architecture of Vaswani et al. (2017). BERT$_{\mathrm{BASE}}$: $L=12$ layers, $H=768$ hidden size, $A=12$ attention heads, 110M parameters. BERT$_{\mathrm{LARGE}}$: $L=24$, $H=1024$, $A=16$, 340M parameters.

nodes.name: Input representation
nodes.statement: The input is a sequence of WordPiece tokens. The first token is always [CLS], whose final hidden state serves as the aggregate sequence representation for classification. Sentence pairs are separated by [SEP]. Each token embedding is the sum of its token embedding, segment embedding (sentence A or B), and position embedding.

nodes.name: Masked Language Model (MLM) pre-training objective
nodes.statement: Randomly mask 15% of input WordPiece tokens. Of the selected positions: 80% are replaced with [MASK], 10% with a random token, 10% kept unchanged. The model predicts the original token at masked positions using a softmax over the vocabulary conditioned on the full bidirectional context. This enables deep bidirectional pre-training, unlike left-to-right language models.

nodes.name: Next Sentence Prediction (NSP) pre-training objective
nodes.statement: A binary classification task: given a pair of sentences (A, B), predict whether B is the actual next sentence of A in the corpus (IsNext) or a randomly sampled sentence (NotNext). 50% positive, 50% negative pairs. The [CLS] token representation is used for prediction.

nodes.name: Fine-tuning procedure
nodes.statement: For each downstream task, add a task-specific output layer on top of pre-trained BERT and fine-tune all parameters end-to-end. For token-level tasks (NER, QA): use per-token hidden states. For sentence-level tasks (classification, inference): use the [CLS] representation. Fine-tuning typically requires 1-3 epochs.

nodes.name: Bidirectionality vs. left-to-right
nodes.statement: Unlike GPT which uses a left-to-right Transformer, and ELMo which concatenates independently trained left-to-right and right-to-left LSTMs, BERT conditions on both left and right context in every layer via the MLM objective. This avoids the 'see itself' problem of standard bidirectional LMs.

nodes.name: Pre-train/fine-tune mismatch mitigation
nodes.statement: The [MASK] token used during pre-training never appears during fine-tuning, creating a mismatch. The 80/10/10 masking strategy (mask/random/unchanged) mitigates this by ensuring the model does not always expect [MASK] at positions it must predict.

nodes.name: State-of-the-art results on 11 NLP tasks
nodes.statement: BERT achieves new state-of-the-art on GLUE (80.5%), MultiNLI (86.7%), SQuAD v1.1 (F1 93.2%), and SQuAD v2.0 (F1 83.1%), outperforming all previous models including GPT and ELMo by large margins.

nodes.name: BERT pre-training procedure
nodes.statement: Pre-train on BooksCorpus (800M words) + English Wikipedia (2500M words) using combined MLM and NSP losses. Use Adam optimizer with learning rate warmup and linear decay. Train for 1M steps with batch size 256 sequences of 512 tokens.
